description:
We are five ambitious first-year students from diverse disciplines: Applied Physics, Applied Chemistry, Computer Engineering, Network Security, and Mechanical Engineering. United by curiosity and creativity, we aim to transform the history of space exploration into an engaging story for younger audiences, combining science, technology, and storytelling to introduce NASA’s missions and inspire the next generation of explorers.

Different disciplines, one passion: turning curiosity into discovery!
summary: We participated in the NASA Space Apps storytelling challenge with a sci-fi mystery narrative powered by authentic NASA data. The story follows a detective and her AI assistant, ELIO, who reopen a mysterious cold case surrounding abandoned space artifacts across the Moon and Mars. Our narrative journey begins at the Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum in Virginia, utilizing precise visual references of the Surveyor 3 camera brought back by Apollo 12. From there, the characters travel past the historic Apollo 11 Eagle lunar module before pushing through a fierce dust storm onto the Martian surface. On Mars, the detective encounters NASA’s legendary rovers—Sojourner, Spirit, and Opportunity—personified as ghostly spirits whispering their historic achievements and water discoveries. By blending real NASA scientific facts with atmospheric detective storytelling, the project honors these silent mechanical sacrifices, concluding under a serene blue Martian sunset with the ultimate question: "Was Mars ever a home?"
details: “The Ghost Within the Scraps” is an illustrated storytelling project developed by a team of five first-year university students from different academic disciplines in response to the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, Abandoned but Not Forgotten. Our project aims to introduce teenagers aged 13–16 to the history of NASA’s space exploration and the stories of its abandoned equipment on the Moon and Mars through an engaging detective adventure. Rather than presenting scientific facts in a traditional educational format, we created a fictional investigation following a young detective and her robotic assistant, ELIO, as they reopen a mysterious cold case involving forgotten space machines. Through their journey across Earth, the Moon, and Mars, readers discover the missions, purposes, challenges, and remarkable scientific contributions of historical spacecraft and rovers, including Surveyor III, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, and other iconic equipment. One of our main creative approaches was personification, giving the forgotten machines ghost-like appearances and voices, allowing them to tell their own stories and creating an emotional connection between readers and the history behind each mission. We combined mystery, humor, scientific dialogue, flashbacks, visual storytelling, and cinematic scene transitions to make complex historical and scientific information accessible without losing its educational value. The project was developed collaboratively, with Toleen serving as the team leader, main author, and screenwriter, responsible for developing the central concept, writing the storyline and dialogues, designing the characters, and coordinating the creative direction. Hala contributed to creating the illustrations using AI-assisted visual tools, bringing the written scenes and characters to life. Nour was responsible for organizing and designing the book, arranging its text and illustrations into a cohesive and visually consistent final product. Ahed contributed to the creative process through brainstorming, storyline development, editing, and research, while Abdalrhman focused on proofreading, language accuracy, and documenting the sources used to support the scientific and historical information. Our team brought together two Applied Physics students, one Applied Chemistry student, one Computer Engineering and Network Security student, and one Mechanical Engineering student, allowing us to combine different perspectives, skills, and ideas. One of our greatest challenges was time, as we had to balance our university responsibilities with researching NASA missions, verifying information, developing an original storyline, writing the screenplay, producing illustrations, and assembling the final book within a limited timeframe. We also had to find the right balance between scientific accuracy and creative storytelling, ensuring that the educational content remained reliable while the narrative stayed exciting and age-appropriate. Despite these challenges, we worked through continuous collaboration, discussions, and revisions to bring our idea together. Ultimately, our goal was not simply to introduce readers to forgotten machines, but to help them understand the significance of their journeys and the discoveries they made possible. Through this story, we hope to inspire young audiences to explore science, question the unknown, and recognize that a mission’s value is not measured only by how long a machine operates or whether it returns home, but also by the knowledge and progress it leaves behind. Because even when a machine falls silent, its story does not have to end. Abandoned, perhaps, but never forgotten.
